ABSTRACT: Asymmetric functionalization of unactivated alkyl-
substituted azaarenes at the α-position of the alkyl substituent is
challenging because deprotonation of the weakly acidic α-C−H
bonds requires a strong base. This requirement often impedes
efective enantiocontrol by chiral catalysts. As a result, the few
reactions that have been reported have narrow substrate scopes.

enantioselective allenylic alkylation reactions of unactivated 2-
alkylbenzoxazoles with conjugated enynes, enabled by synergistic
borane/nickel catalysis. The success of this method hinges on
catalytic activation of the 2-alkylbenzoxazoles by a triarylborane,

reaction, we investigated its substrate scope (Table 2).
Replacement of the 2-ethyl group in 1a with <sup>n</sup>propyl, <sup>n</sup>pentyl,
or phenethyl groups aforded products 3b−3d in good yields
with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivities. When

and diastereoselectivity, afording product 3e in 20% yield and
1.5:1 dr, while maintaining high ee values for both
diastereomers. The use of 2-methylbenzoxazole also resulted
in a low yield of the desired product (3f, 29%) along with a
dialkylation byproduct in 10% yield (not shown in Table 2). In
contrast, when the <sup>i</sup>propyl or cyclopentyl group was positioned
one carbon further along the alkyl chain, the reactions
proceeded smoothly to give 3g and 3h in high yields.
Furthermore, 2-alkyl chains bearing terminal ester, trifluor-
omethyl, phenoxy, acetoxy, or benzoyloxy substituent were
well tolerated, afording products 3i−3m in 54−94% yields
with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivities (up to >20:1
dr and 99% ee). The diastereo- and enantioselectivity
remained high across a range of benzoxazoles bearing diverse
aryl ring substituents at various positions (3n−3v). Notably,
benzoxazoles bearing ester substituents (1q and 1t) failed to
furnish the corresponding products (3q and 3t) under
conditions without LA1, indicating that the ester group
could not provide the same activation as the borane catalyst.
Aryl-substituted enynes bearing various electron-donating or
electron-withdrawing groups at the ortho, meta, or para
position of the benzene ring were compatible with the reaction
conditions; products 4b−4h were obtained in 65−89% yields
with high diastereo- and enantioselectivities. 2-Naphthyl-, 3-
thienyl-, and alkyl-substituted enynes also underwent the
reaction, afording target products 4i−4l with high diastereo-
and enantioselectivities. The absolute configuration of 4m was
determined by X-ray crystallography of a single crystal. The
scope of this reaction is presently confined to benzoxazoles
(see the Supporting Information for incompatible heteroar-
enes).
The allenylic alkylation reaction was readily scaled up: the
reaction of 1a (5.0 mmol) with 2l (10.0 mmol) aforded 4l in
84% yield with 11:1 dr and 99% ee (Scheme 2). Desilylation of
4l with tetrabutylammonium fluoride provided 5 in 82% yield.
Subsequent gold-catalyzed intramolecular cyclization<sup>3c,12</sup> of 5
via hydroxyl attack on the allene furnished 6 in 78% yield as
the E-olefin exclusively, with retention of both dr and ee. In
contrast, N-iodosuccinimide-mediated cyclization<sup>13</sup> of 5 gave 7

■ CONCLUSIONS
In conclusion, we used synergistic borane/transition metal
catalysis to overcome the challenges posed by asymmetric
functionalization of unactivated alkylazaarenes at the α-
position of the alkyl substituent. This strategy allowed us to
achieve the first examples of coupling reactions between
unactivated 2-alkylbenzoxazoles and conjugated enynes, which
were promoted by a borane/nickel catalytic system and
aforded previously elusive compounds with 1,3-nonadjacent
stereocenters. Moreover, diastereo- and enantioselective
asymmetric allylic alkylation reactions of unactivated 2-
alkylbenzoxazoles with acyclic 1,3-disubstituted allylic esters
were achieved with a borane/palladium system. A key element
of both transformations is the use of fluorinated triarylboranes,
which enable base-mediated deprotonation of otherwise poorly
acidic α-C−H bonds under mild conditions. The method has a
broad substrate scope, allowing reactions of diverse 2-
alkylbenzoxazoles and electrophiles (>60 examples). Our
work not only provides powerful solutions for accessing
complex chiral architectures bearing multiple stereocenters
from readily available precursors but also establishes synergistic
borane/transition metal catalysis as a versatile strategy for
asymmetric functionalization reactions.
